lines.text: Three side lengths are given, but you only need ONE!
lines.caption: Three side lengths are given, but you only need ONE!

lines.text: Can you spot the hidden triangle?
lines.caption: Can you spot the hidden triangle?

lines.text: A B and A C are ten. B C is twelve.
lines.caption: A B and A C are ten. B C is twelve.

lines.text: A line through A is parallel to B C. The bisector of angle B meets it at F.
lines.caption: A line through A is parallel to B C. The bisector of angle B meets it at F.

lines.text: The bisector splits angle B into two equal parts. Call each part x.
lines.caption: The bisector splits angle B into two equal parts. Call each part x.

lines.text: Now find the Z. The parallel lines make the angle at F equal x too.
lines.caption: Now find the Z. The parallel lines make the angle at F equal x too.

lines.text: So triangle A B F has two equal angles, and A F equals A B!
lines.caption: So triangle A B F has two equal angles, and A F equals A B!

lines.text: A B is ten, so A F is ten!
lines.caption: A B is ten, so A F is ten!

lines.text: The other two sides were just decoys.
lines.caption: The other two sides were just decoys.

lines.text: Why equal sides? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why equal sides? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
